text:
[title] PagedAttention + speculative decoding: 2.4x goodput at p99
[body] KV-cache fragmentation: <4% waste via block tables
[body] Draft model acceptance alpha = 0.78 at gamma = 5
[body] Continuous batching; chunked prefill off to hold the TTFT SLO

novice.takeaway: The presenter combined several technical methods (memory management, speculative decoding, batching) to achieve a 2.4x improvement in system throughput/performance at the 99th percentile.
questions: What is the TTFT SLO threshold?
Why does turning chunked prefill off help?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe these specific technical optimizations caused the claimed 2.4x performance gain.

peer.takeaway: Combining memory-efficient attention with speculative decoding techniques achieves a 2.4x throughput gain at p99 latency by reducing memory waste and tuning batching settings.
questions: What is PagedAttention's block table mechanism exactly?
What do alpha and gamma parameters represent?
Why disable chunked prefill to meet TTFT SLO?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe their system design choices jointly deliver the 2.4x goodput improvement.

expert.takeaway: Combining PagedAttention with speculative decoding achieves 2.4x p99 goodput by cutting KV-cache fragmentation and using tuned draft acceptance with continuous batching.
questions: Why is chunked prefill turned off, not just tuned?
What baseline is the 2.4x goodput measured against?
What model sizes/hardware were used for gamma=5 test?
expert.inferred_claim: These specific system choices (block tables, speculative decoding params, batching config) jointly produce the claimed 2.4x gain.
